thread:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding magnet-16b-int8. Saw weird behavior when we prefill ~12k tokens and then hand off to streaming: repetition spike + token dropouts around token 11874.

raj: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro?

maya: repro attached inline: run with --prefill=12000 --quant=int8 --rope-scale=1.0. observed on dedicated-staging GPU pool.

maya: command:
```
python run_infer.py --model magnet-16b-int8 --prefill 12000 --prompt-file tests/longprefill/anchor.txt --streaming True --kv-mode warmstart
```

olivia: logs? stack traces?

maya: relevant snippet from stdout (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-20 14:32:01] prefill: wrote 12000 tokens to kv cache (shard0)
[2026-03-20 14:32:01] kv_handshake: warmstart ok, seq=12000
[2026-03-20 14:32:02] generate: step=11870 token=...
[2026-03-20 14:32:02] generate: step=11871 token=<REPETITION_START>
[2026-03-20 14:32:02] kv_lookup: missed index 11871 -> fallback to fresh compute
[2026-03-20 14:32:02] generate: step=11872 token=<DROPPED_TOKEN>
```

tom: kv_lookup missed index — that screams off-by-one in our prefill stride or a shard boundary. did the prefill cross a shard?

maya: yes prefill spanned shard0->shard1 boundary; our shard size 16384 so it crossed internal rotate.

raj: could be RoPE position wrap mismatch between quantized and fp32 kernels. if int8 uses different RoPE scaling or rounding, indices can drift.

olivia: did you try changing rope-scale to 0.999 or 1.001?

maya: tried 0.999 — reduced repetition but still had one dropout at 11990. rope-scale=1.001 made it worse.

maya: i also replayed the same prefill but with quant=int16 (no quant) — no dropouts, clean streaming handoff. so quantization seems implicated.

raj: hypothesis: quantized KV store uses compressed index packing that rounds during memcpy. Combined with rotary scaling normalization we can get an alignment slip at shard handshake.

olivia: can you capture the raw kv key vectors at index ~11860-11900 on both shards before and after handoff? we should diff floats vs dequantized ints.

maya: grabbing dumps now. dumping to /tmp/magnet16b-dumps/1812349999/*.bin

ciara-bot: perf-tests queue updated: magnet16b-longprefill-handshake (run id: 20260320-14-40).

tom: also run with --kv-mode=copy rather than warmstart to verify if handshake protocol is the issue. if copy avoids it then handshake path is likely buggy.

maya: ran copy mode — no issues. warmstart -> failure. confirmed.

raj: ok that narrows it. can you paste the kv handshake payload sizes and the crc checks?

maya: handshake metadata: shard0->shard1 transfer bytes=3,456,128, crc=0x7a2b4c; shard1 ack crc=0x7a2b4c; but after dequant we see key[11871] mismatch (hamming distance low but floats differ by 0.0024 relative).

olivia: 0.0024 relative is suspiciously like quant scale mismatch. what quant library? q8hug or custom?

maya: using our onboard int8 path (qscale-v2). config: {"zero_point":"symmetric","per_channel":true,"scale_bits":8}.

raj: try toggling per_channel=false to see if per-channel scaling rounding across shards causes different effective scales.

maya: toggled per_channel=false — reran warmstart — no failure. so per_channel true + handshake seems to have rounding inconsistency across shards.

tom: maybe metadata for scales wasn't being serialized consistently during handshake (we only include global metadata currently). check the handshake payload — are per-channel scale arrays included?

maya: we only send a single scale vector in handshake payload for bandwidth reasons. seems we accidentally rely on local recompute of per-channel scales during warmstart which can differ by a tiny epsilon.

raj: that explains it. epsilon accumulates at boundary and with RoPE rotations magnifies into token diffs.

olivia: mitigation options: 1) include full per-channel scales in handshake (bigger payload), 2) force deterministic recompute (seed + algorithm), 3) fallback to copy mode for warmstarts crossing shards > threshold.

maya: i prototyped option 2: deterministic recompute fixes in 90% of runs. still want to ship option1 for correctness but need perf tradeoff.

tom: what's rollout plan? we need a quick fix before the magnet16b public onboard.

maya: propose hotfix: if prefill crosses shard boundary and quant.per_channel true -> force kv-mode=copy for that session + alert. then schedule handshake metadata expansion in next patch.

raj: sounds reasonable. also add unit test that does cross-shard warmstart with per-channel scaling and asserts bitwise-equal dequantized keys.

olivia: + add an eval comparing generation perplexity and repetition rate between warmstart vs copy for longprefill workloads. baseline int16 should be reference.

maya: created GH issue #4523, assigned to eng-ml and eng-runtime. I pushed a small change to detect crossing boundary and flip kv-mode. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/7821

ciara-bot: PR 7821 status: CI started (unit tests + perf smoke).

maya: i'll keep collecting dumps and perf traces. ping me if you want to run reproducer on dedicated-staging (tag me).

tom: thanks. can we add a short note in onboarding doc: "magnet-16b-int8: avoid warmstart crossing shard boundaries until metadata handshake expanded"?

maya: added a draft to docs/onboarding/notes.md on the repo.

raj: great triage. follow-up: schedule a full quant-handshake design meeting tomorrow. i'll set a calendar invite. :calendar:
